analogy.boundary: The comparison stops at when a transfer may be called done; it says nothing about whether every other transfer can be reversed.

maps.analogy: the bank's ability to reverse the transfer
the transfer marked final and non-refundable
maps.doctrine: a declared point of no return

maps.analogy: the starting balance being unchanged when the next leg runs
maps.doctrine: the check that the expected starting state is still current

maps.analogy: no second transfer touching the same account at the same time
maps.doctrine: the rule of one writer per path

analogy.text: A bank transfer completes only if the bank can reverse it or has marked it final. A transfer in several legs goes ahead only while the starting balance is unchanged and no other transfer is touching the same account.

reader.counterexample: A step writes to a shared path and is counted as complete because the call returned, with no check of the starting state and no single-writer rule, so two writers interleave and the result matches neither.
reader.does_not_prove: Only the named paths reject a changed starting state or a second writer, and the registry records that linking these failure cases to the full rule is still unchecked.

example.text: The mission transaction work spine completes a change in several steps only when the starting state it expected is still the current one, so a run whose starting state was replaced in the meantime fails with a parent-mismatch error instead of overwriting the newer state.

reader.governs: When a change to stored state may be counted as complete.
reader.plain: A change only counts as done if there is a stated way to undo it, or a clear note that it can never be undone. A change in several steps goes ahead only if its expected starting point is unchanged and nobody else is changing the same thing.
reader.potential_misread: That every change must be reversible, when a change may also be declared permanent so long as it says which it is.
reader.refuses: An irreversible write made without these checks.
reader.requires: An undo step or a declared point of no return, and for changes in several steps, a check that the expected starting state is still current plus a rule that only one writer works on a path at a time.
reader.why_it_matters: A half-finished change cannot be counted as complete, which is how a system ends up in a state nobody chose and nobody can reverse.

data.statement:
Formal clause: an effect requires a compensator or declared irreversible
boundary; multi-step effects land as a saga with compare-and-swap and
single-writer constraints.

Lineage: ACID, saga pattern, optimistic concurrency control.

Route: recorded as strongly witnessed by `mission_transaction_work_spine`,
`durable_agent_work_landing_replay`, `concurrency_mission_control`, the
work-landing tools and mission preflight. The tests block a change whose
parent commit does not match, two claims on the same path, and a change with
no evidence that the branch head moved.

Anti-axiom: an irreversible write is made with no way to undo it.
